## Summary

Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron main process: init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap, graceful degradation when Steam is absent, and a minimal preload context-bridge API so the renderer never touches the SDK directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `electron/main.ts` initialises Steamworks (with `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary` + app ID bootstrap, e.g. `steam_appid.txt`) and logs a clear warning when Steam is unavailable.
- [ ] The launcher boots and is fully functional without Steam (dev / non-Steam runs) — no crash, web app unaffected (intake AC5).
- [ ] `electron/preload.ts` exposes a minimal `steamFollow` API via contextBridge: `isSteamAvailable`, `openStorePage(appId)`, `isFollowing(devAccountId)`, `claim(...)` (as confirmed by F1).
- [ ] Renderer code has zero direct Steam SDK imports (enforced by F2's interface contract).
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds with the Steamworks native module packaging config (Windows primary target per launcher item).
- [ ] All F2 unit tests still pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Steamworks init module behind the `FollowSource` interface (F2).
- Preload context bridge exposing `steamFollow`.
- electron-builder config updated for the native module (Windows primary).

## Dependencies

- F2 (interface contract).
- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (launcher provides electron/main.ts, electron/preload.ts structure).

## Deliverables

- `electron/main.ts` Steamworks init, `electron/preload.ts` bridge, packaging config.

data.description:
# Render card SVGs at native resolution instead of 4x quality upsampling

## Problem statement

`rasteriseSvgToTexture()` in `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` hard-codes a 4x
oversampling factor (`qualityScale = Math.max(4, dpr)`). Every card SVG is
therefore rasterised at 4x its logical size (a 140x80 card becomes a 560x320
canvas) regardless of the device pixels it actually occupies, wasting ~16x
texture memory / GPU upload bandwidth and forcing the embedded 64x64 art zone
onto a 256x256 device-pixel region.

## Users

- **Engine/rendering maintainer** — wants the shared SVG texture helper to
  allocate textures at the resolution they are displayed, without changing
  public APIs or texture-key semantics.
  - As a rendering maintainer, I want `rasteriseSvgToTexture()` to scale by
    device density (with a small quality floor) so that card textures no longer
    over-allocate memory.
  - As a game developer consuming `@core-engine`, I want the change to be
    transparent — same texture keys, same placeholder-to-raster flow, no visual
    regression — so I do not have to update per-game code.
  - As a mobile/low-memory player, I want cards to render crisply at my
    display density without the engine uploading 16x more pixels than needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `rasteriseSvgToTexture()` no longer hard-codes a 4x multiplier; the render
   scale is `qualityScale = Math.max(MIN_QUALITY_SCALE, dpr)` where
   `MIN_QUALITY_SCALE = 2` is a named, documented constant. Verified by unit
   tests asserting the resulting canvas dimensions for DPR 1, 2 and 3.
2. Both the placeholder canvas (when registered) and the final rasterised
   canvas use the same scale, and equal
   `round(width * qualityScale) x round(height * qualityScale)` — e.g. a
   140x80 logical card yields 280x160 at DPR 1 and 2, and 420x240 at DPR 3.
   Verified by a test asserting canvas dimensions at each DPR.
3. Texture cache keys are unchanged (`makeTextureKey` still encodes logical
   size + DPR, no qualityScale), so no key fragmentation; existing
   `makeTextureKey` tests continue to pass.
4. Visual review at DPR 1, 2 and 3 confirms no legibility regression in card
   text / vector strokes versus the 4x baseline; reviewer sign-off is recorded
   on this work item.
5. `SvgHelpers` unit and browser tests are updated to the new resolution
   contract (the `>= 4x` assertion in `tests/core-engine/SvgHelpers.test.ts`
   is removed/replaced).
6. Card textures are allocated at native display resolution: with
   `MIN_QUALITY_SCALE = 2` the 256x256 embedded art
   (CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R) is always downscaled, never upscaled, so pixelation
   cannot return; verified by the canvas-dimension tests plus the visual
   review.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments (`SvgHelpers.ts` JSDoc) and the `docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Card art
   pipeline" section.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No public API signature changes; `makeTextureKey` key format and the
  placeholder-then-raster lifecycle (no flicker/black frames) must be preserved.
- The change is a memory optimisation — visual legibility must not regress.
- Applies uniformly to all `SvgHelpers` consumers (Main Street, Lost Cities,
  The Mind, Gym); no per-game overrides or bespoke rasterisation.
- Headless / test / reduced-motion paths remain unaffected.

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` — `qualityScale = Math.max(4, dpr)`,
  `targetW = Math.round(width * qualityScale)` (placeholder and final canvas).
- Consumers: `src/ui/Renderer/renderCardSvg.ts`, `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSvgHelpersScene.ts`,
  and the game renderers that call `getOrCreateTexture`.
- `tests/core-engine/SvgHelpers.test.ts` currently asserts 10x20 @ DPR 2 =>
  40x80 (the 4x contract).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` "Card art pipeline (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN,
  CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R)" documents the 4x scale and the 256x256 WebP embedded
  art (already shipped).

## Desired change

Introduce a single documented scale resolver
(`qualityScale = Math.max(2, dpr)`, floor as a named constant) and use it for
both the placeholder and final canvases. Update the JSDoc, the `DEVELOPER.md`
pipeline section, and the tests to the native-resolution contract. Chosen
interpretation: option C — DPR-matched with a small supersample floor
(producer-confirmed; see Appendix).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts` — replace the hard-coded 4x with a documented
  `Math.max(MIN_QUALITY_SCALE, dpr)` helper (applied to placeholder + final
  canvas); update JSDoc.
- `tests/core-engine/SvgHelpers.test.ts` — replace the ">= 4x" assertion with
  DPR 1/2/3 canvas-dimension assertions.
- `tests/core-engine/SvgHelpers.browser.test.ts` — assert the generated
  texture's source dimensions (browser integration).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — rewrite the "Card art pipeline" resolution paragraph
  (`qualityScale = Math.max(4, dpr)` => `Math.max(2, dpr)`; 256x256 device-px
  claim).
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymSvgHelpersScene.ts` — only if its
  rasterisation comment references the old scale.

## Related work

- **CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R** (completed) — raised embedded card art to 256x256
  WebP; complementary: this change lowers the required art resolution while the
  art change keeps the card crisp at any rasterisation scale.
- **CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN** — card art pipeline (source sprites, generator,
  docs).
- The final embedded-art resolution decision (64/128/256) is a follow-up to
  CG-0MUCM36EQ008YP4R; keep it out of scope here.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP17N07X006KLA1** – Fix skipped lower card not removed after out-of-turn play in The Mind (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MQJT28MF007CRA5** – Playtest: Gym — Lighting Spike (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mucm36eq008yp4r, acceptance, actually, art, artefacts (+108 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, actually, art, becomes, browser (+79 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mucm36eq008yp4r, actually, art, browser, build (+68 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — DPR 1 legibility:** a floor of 2 still halves the old baseline at
  DPR 1. Mitigation: AC4 visual review; the floor is a named constant that can
  be raised (e.g. 2.5 / 3) if review shows artefacts.
- **Risk — stale over-allocated textures in a live SPA session:** cache keys do
  not encode qualityScale, so textures created before the change survive until
  a reload. Mitigation: documented as a reload-cleared cache; no code change.
- **Risk — placeholder / final canvas divergence:** a missed call site would
  register a texture whose backing canvas size differs. Mitigation: AC2 and a
  single shared scale helper, asserted by canvas-dimension tests.
- **Assumption — interpretation:** "native resolution" means the display
  native (DPR-matched) resolution with a small supersample floor (option C),
  confirmed by the producer.
- **Assumption — floor value:** `MIN_QUALITY_SCALE = 2` (lowest integer
  supersample in the offered 1.5x-2x range), documented and tunable.
- **Scope-creep risk:** deciding the final embedded-art resolution and any
  per-game rasterisation overrides are separate work — record as linked work
  items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "In `rasteriseSvgToTexture()`, what should 'native resolution' mean for the
  replacement of `qualityScale = Math.max(4, dpr)`?" — Options: (A) DPR-matched
  (`qualityScale = dpr`); (B) higher intrinsic SVG canvas rasterised 1:1;
  (C) DPR-matched with a small supersample floor `Math.max(S, dpr)`.
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **C**. Source: interactive reply
  (session `herdr-1790695176-1359644-7436`). Follow-up assumption recorded by
  Map: floor `S = 2` (`MIN_QUALITY_SCALE`), documented and tunable.
- Q: "Are you saying C is better quality?" — Answer (Map): C is not
  unconditionally better; it is a quality-vs-memory trade-off, marginally
  better for thin strokes/small text at the cost of some of the memory win.
  Source: interactive reply. (Clarification only; the producer's choice
  remained C.)
data.title: Render card SVGs at native resolution instead of 4x quality upsampling

## Summary

The F1-approved follow-detection mechanism — `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(developerSteamID)` — is **not exposed** by `steamworks.js`, the only maintained npm binding for the Steamworks SDK (verified: v0.4.0 exposes achievement/apps/auth/cloud/input/localplayer/matchmaking/networking/overlay/stats/utils/workshop namespaces, but **no `friends` namespace**).

As a result, the launcher shipped on CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC implements:
- real SDK store-page opening via `overlay.activateToStore` / `activateToWebPage`,
- real Steamworks init (`init` + `restartAppIfNecessary` + app id bootstrap),
- follow detection **capability-detected**: `followCheckSupported = false` when the binding lacks the API, with a persisted **manual self-attest claim** fallback.

This delivers the feature with graceful degradation, but does **not** achieve fully automatic follow detection.

## Desired outcome

Automatic follow detection that survives an audit of intake AC2 ("the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks"), via one of:

- (a) A small **custom native addon** wrapping `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` (N-API), shipped alongside `steamworks.js`; the existing `SteamworksClientLike.friends.isFollowing` seam means no TypeScript change is needed once present.
- (b) A newer `steamworks.js` release (or a fork) that exposes `friends.isFollowing`.
- (c) A publisher-backend Steam Web API check (needs a server component; previously scoped out).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A concrete mechanism exposing `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` is available to the Electron main process.
- [ ] `SteamworksFollowSource.followCheckSupported` becomes `true` on a real Steam session and automatic unlock is verified end-to-end with a real Steam account.
- [ ] No regression to the graceful-degradation path (absent module → unavailable, no crash).
- [ ] Automated tests cover the new detection path with a fake module.

## Relationship

Discovered while implementing CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (F3). Follow-up, not a blocker: the shipped feature degrades to a manual claim.
data.title: Steam follow detection: expose ISteamFriends::IsFollowing via a native addon or newer binding

## F3 finding — Steamworks binding has no follow-detection API

While wiring the real Steamworks adapter I verified the only maintained npm binding, `steamworks.js` v0.4.0: it exposes `achievement`, `apps`, `auth`, `callback`, `cloud`, `input`, `localplayer`, `matchmaking`, `networking`, `overlay`, `stats`, `utils`, `workshop` — but **no `friends` namespace**, so `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` is unavailable.

What exists and is used:
- `overlay.activateToStore(appId, StoreFlag)` / `overlay.activateToWebPage(url)` — real SDK store-page opening.
- `init(appId)` + `restartAppIfNecessary(appId)` + `electronEnableSteamOverlay()` — Steamworks bootstrap.

Consequence: follow detection is **capability-detected**. `SteamworksFollowSource.followCheckSupported` is `false` with the current binding; the UI offers a persisted manual self-attest claim, and the launcher never fabricates a `true`. Automatic detection is tracked as a follow-up: CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1 (discovered-from this item).
